title: Dipeptidyl peptidase IV in angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor associated angioedema
authors: Byrd JB, Touzin K, Sile S, Gainer JV, Yu C, Nadeau J, et al.
population: 50 people with a history of ACE-inhibitor-associated angio-oedema and 176 ACE-inhibitor-exposed controls without angio-oedema
funder: not read: the available full-text record contains only the abstract and disclosures; PubMed indexes the work as NIH extramural research support.
authorConflicts: Brown is a consultant for Novartis, one of several companies developing a DPP-4 inhibitor, and holds a patent for identifying susceptibility to ACE-inhibitor angio-oedema.
result: Serum DPP-4 activity (26.6 against 29.6 nmol/ml per minute, P=0.026) and antigen (465.8 against 563.1 ng/ml, P=0.017) were lower in cases than controls; during ACE inhibition the difference was larger (activity 21.5 against 29.8, P=0.001), but not in the absence of ACE inhibition. The ex vivo degradation half-life of substance P correlated inversely with DPP-4 antigen during ACE inhibition. Bradykinin and substance P, both ACE substrates, increase vascular permeability in animals.
